text:
The best matching location for the farm's future climate is Gilliam County, Oregon, sharing a strong match quality where 8 out of 8 climate models agree. The sigma value measures how different a place's climate today is from the farm's future climate, in units of the farm's normal year-to-year swings, where lower means closer. 

Zero matching areas use the field's current rotation. The rotations used at the matching places are winter wheat to fallow and continuous winter wheat. 

Comparing hazards with the best match, the field and match today both have 32 days above 32 degrees Celsius per year. The frost-free season has 164 days at the field today and 192 days at the match. For afternoon ground temperature in June, the field is 41.1 degrees Celsius while the match is 39.7 degrees Celsius. For July-August afternoon ground temperature, the field is 46.4 degrees Celsius and the match is 46.5 degrees Celsius. The driest-month soil water in September is 17.8 percent at the field and 19.2 percent at the match. 

Overall, temperatures are projected to increase across the year alongside varying changes in precipitation under middle-of-the-road emissions. These results are based on 3351 farmland cells.
